sources_considered.why: Primary announcement of a market study. It measures enterprise spending rather than the complete market asserted in the claim.
Read the analyst report. Its new-application revenue estimate has a narrower boundary than all AI demand and does not measure subsidy dependence. The extracted columns also interleave.
Read the working-paper summary. Compensation required to give up existing access is not observed demand at a verified cost-covering price.
Read relevant passages; the cleaner primary announcement was used for quotation. Neither source supplies the required supplier costs.

evidence_items.locator: Main announcement, paragraph beginning Applications captured
evidence_items.explanation: The study separates application spending from infrastructure and estimates enterprise spending using survey and market data. Its narrower market and absence of supplier-cost measurements prevent it from settling either the aggregate $65 billion assertion or universal subsidy dependence.

metric_scope.company: Enterprise generative AI application providers, industry subset
metric_scope.metric: Estimated annual enterprise spending on AI applications

unresolved_gaps: No consistently bounded total was established for the precise market meant by the speaker.
The market estimate was published before the end of 2025 and is not an audited final-year total.
No matched cost-and-demand evidence establishes universal subsidy dependence.
No observed industry-wide sustainable-price intervention was established.
Customer value, actual payment, provider gross margin, and fully cost-covering profitability remain distinct measurements.
